discord.label: Discord username
discord.unverifiedHint: Unverified tag: {audience} Verify it so they can.
discord.unverifiedAudience: nobody sees it, not even the administrators. So the organizers can't reach you during a tournament.
discord.audience: the administrators see it at any time, the referees as long as you're registered for a tournament that isn't over (from the moment registration opens), the members of both teams of your match from the moment both its opponents are known until its end, and its caster only while the match is being played (and, if you cast a match, both its teams and the referees, only while the match is being played); other players only if you make it visible in your privacy settings. Nobody else, ever.

privacy.pseudoAlwaysVisible: Your username is always visible: it's what identifies you in brackets, rosters and match sheets.
privacy.discordNotice: Verification opens your Discord tag to the organizers (administrators at any time, referees as long as you're registered for a tournament that isn't over) and, as a contact, to the members of both teams of your match from the moment both its opponents are known, and to its caster only while the match is being played (and, if you cast a match, to both its teams and the referees while the match is being played); not to other players: tick “Discord tag” so they can see it on your profile. An unverified tag stays hidden, box ticked or not.
privacy.discordPending: Your tag isn't verified: it will stay hidden from other players until you verify it.
privacy.discordNoTag: You don't have a Discord tag yet: save it, then verify it so other players can see it.
privacy.recruitmentHint: Unticked by default. Ticked, you show up in the directory's “Free agents” filter and your card says “FREE AGENT” as long as you have no team.

accountLocale.label: Notification language
accountLocale.hint: Push notifications reach you in this language. It follows the page's language each time you log in: your choice here holds until you next log in from a page in the other language.

matchDms.label: Discord direct messages about my matches
matchDms.notCertified: These messages only go to accounts with a verified Discord tag, to avoid spam: without a verified tag, they can't reach you.
matchDms.hint: On by default: the bot messages you privately when one of your matches is scheduled, rescheduled or unscheduled, when a match leaves your schedule, and for its reminders (day before, check-in). Untick to stop receiving them: your push notifications keep their own settings, and referees still get theirs.
matchDms.enabledNotCertified: Match direct messages turned on: they'll be sent once your Discord tag is verified.

deletion.question: Permanently delete your account?
deletion.residual: As with any deleted account, what remains is: the site's encrypted backups ({backupDays} days), the record of your deletion in the log used to replay it after a restore (at least {journalDays} days), the audience-measurement fingerprint described in the privacy policy, your connection data (IP address, date, login method), which the law requires us to keep for {logDays} days, the announcements of your solo-tournament matches posted in the Discord #live channel (and the moderation alert for an announcement blocked or flagged by AutoMod), which keep your username until they are deleted on request, and, if you're a staff member, the trace of your actions in the server logs.

consequences.TOURNAMENTS: Your personal information will be erased and your username replaced with a placeholder one, but your tournament statistics will be kept — they also belong to the teams you played against.
consequences.SOLO_REGISTRATIONS: Your personal information will be erased and your username replaced with a placeholder one, but your record will remain: you're registered for a solo tournament, where your username serves as the entrant's name and will be replaced by that placeholder.
consequences.ORGANIZED_TOURNAMENTS: Your personal information will be erased and your username replaced with a placeholder one, but your record will remain: you're the organizer of tournaments that must keep an owner.
consequences.OWNED_TEAMS: Your personal information will be erased and your username replaced with a placeholder one, but your record will remain: you own a team that nobody could manage without you. Transfer or disband it first for a complete erasure.
consequences.NONE: You haven't played any match and you manage no team or tournament: your account and profile will be erased entirely.
consequences.UNKNOWN: The site couldn't tell what will remain: depending on what you left behind (a match played, a solo tournament registration, a team owned, a tournament organized), it will be anonymized or erased entirely.

outcome.TOURNAMENTS: Account deleted. Your statistics are kept under a placeholder username.
outcome.SOLO_REGISTRATIONS: Account deleted. Your solo tournament registrations now carry a placeholder username.
outcome.ORGANIZED_TOURNAMENTS: Account deleted. Your tournaments keep an anonymous organizer.
outcome.OWNED_TEAMS: Account deleted. Your team keeps an anonymous owner.
outcome.NONE: Account erased. Your account and profile are gone from the site; only the traces described in the privacy policy and its register remain (backups, deletion log, audience measurement).

connections.intro: Your account has no password: it opens through the apps linked below. You can add several so you're never locked out — the last one can't be removed.

notes.GOOGLE: One-click login. No email address is saved.
notes.DISCORD: Login, verification of your tag, and match time notices and reminders by direct message.
notes.BLIZZARD: Login, and your BattleTag kept up to date by Blizzard. You can hide your BattleTag: it then only stays visible in the “Contacts” window of your tournament matches, if you're among the contacts shown: to both teams and the referees from the moment both opponents are known, and to the caster while the match is being played. If you don't want them to see it, remove it from your profile (if it comes from Battle.net, unlink your Battle.net account first — after adding another way to sign in if it is your only one).

battletagNotice.warning: You can hide your BattleTag: it then only stays visible in the “Contacts” window of your tournament matches, if you're among the contacts shown: to both teams and the referees from the moment both opponents are known, and to the caster while the match is being played. If you don't want them to see it, remove it from your profile (if it comes from Battle.net, unlink your Battle.net account first — after adding another way to sign in if it is your only one).
battletagNotice.title: Hidden, but not from everyone
battletagNotice.intro: Your BattleTag will no longer appear anywhere — profile, directory, rosters —, not even to referees and administrators. It stays readable only in a match's “Contacts” window, where it's needed to add each other in game:
battletagNotice.players: The members of both teams of your match, from the moment both its opponents are known to its end, if you're among the contacts shown — it's how you add each other in game to start the match.
battletagNotice.caster: The caster of your match, only while the match is being played (from its start to its end), if you're among the contacts shown.
battletagNotice.asCaster: Both teams and the referees of a match you cast, only while the match is being played (from its start to its end).
battletagNotice.staff: Referees and administrators, in the same “Contacts” window of the tournament's matches, at the same times as both teams — never anywhere else.
battletagNotice.outro: To stop sharing it entirely, you have to clear the field — but your opponents will then no longer be able to add you in game. And if a Blizzard account is linked, it controls this field: you have to remove it first.

verify.title: Verify my Discord tag
verify.purpose: The organizers need to be able to reach you during a tournament: rescheduling a round, a score dispute, a forfeit.
verify.intro: {purpose} Verification is optional and only happens through this step — logging in with Discord doesn't grant it: without it, your tag stays invisible to everyone, administrators included.
verify.matchDms: It also lets the bot send you direct messages about your matches (times, reminders): without it, the bot sends you none.

exposure.admins: The site's administrators can see your Discord tag at all times.
exposure.referees: Referees can see it only while you're entered in an ongoing or upcoming tournament — not after —, or while a match you cast is being played.
exposure.match: The members of both teams of your match can see it from the moment both its opponents are known until its end, and its caster only while the match is being played (from its start to its end) — to add each other and create the channel. If you cast a match, both its teams and the referees see yours only while the match is being played.
exposure.players: Other players on the site only see it if you make it visible in your privacy settings. It doesn't appear on any public page.
exposure.undo: You can cancel at any time by removing your tag from “My profile”: the verification is lost, and the exposure with it. Logging in with Discord then saves your username again, but without verifying it: only this step verifies it.

verify.attested: Username provided by Discord at your last login: {tag}. You just need to confirm — no code, no new Discord authorization.
verify.linkedNoTag: Your account is linked to Discord, but no username provided by Discord is saved. Go through its authorization page, with the Discord account already linked: it will provide your username, which you can then verify here in one click. A username made only of digits can't be verified.
verify.tagHelp: The bot must share a server with you to find your account: <join>join the BlueGenji server</join> before verifying. You'll receive a six-digit code by direct message.
verify.codeHelp: Five attempts, then the code is burned — request a new one if you make a mistake.
verify.codeSent: Code sent by Discord direct message (expires at {time}).

botHandle.intro: Enter your Discord username: the BlueGenji bot sends you a six-digit code by direct message, and the code proves this username is yours.
botHandle.introUpdate: Only the username of the Discord account already linked is accepted.
botHandle.introOutro: A username that changes loses its verification: you can restore it in one click with “Verify my tag”.
botHandle.matchDms: Without verification, the bot sends you no match direct messages.
botHandle.handleHelp: The bot must share a server with you: <join>join the BlueGenji server</join> if you haven't already.
botHandle.codeHelp: Five attempts, then the code is burned — request a new one if you make a mistake.
botHandle.certifyForDms: Verify your tag (Discord section): without verification, no match direct message reaches you.
botHandle.codeSent: Code sent by Discord direct message (expires at {time}).
